dmp.description:
Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a severe inflammatory bowel disease affecting 5-12% of very low birth weight infants. The
associated morbidity is very high being one of the first causes of neonatal short bowel syndrome and a known risk factor
for neurological sequelae in preterm patients.
This project aims to demonstrate that CBD will be at least as effective as the usual empirical antibiotherapy or could even
have a synergistic effect with it, decreasing the associated histological injury and improving inflammation and cell
apoptosis data by studying the modulation in transcription, translation and activity of proteins hypothetically modified by
CBD in our model, which could point to CNB as a possible therapeutic strategy for neonates with NEC.
